chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan ibn Sadeer, from his father, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Do you pray the optional prayers while you are seated?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'I do not pray them except while seated, since I gained this much weight and reached this age.'

key_terms.حَمَلْتُ هَذَا اللَّحْمَ: Gained this much weight (idiom for aging/physical change)

ai.seo_question: Why does the Imam pray optional prayers while seated?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the practical application of concession (*rukhsah*) by praying optional (*nafl*) prayers while seated, attributing his posture to the physical burden of age and weight. This establishes a precedent in Shia jurisprudence that the permissibility of seated prayer extends beyond acute illness to include the natural frailty of old age, emphasizing ease over rigid formality in voluntary worship. The phrase 'gained this flesh' reflects the scholarly understanding that physical heaviness and reduced mobility are valid grounds for modifying the posture of prayer.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan Bin Sadeyr, from his father who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘Are youasws praying the optional Salāt while youasws are seated?’ So heasws said: ‘Iasws have not prayed it except while seated until after Iasws have gained this much weight and reaching this age’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hanan ibn Sadir from his father who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’Do you perform optional Salah (prayer) in a sitting position? He (the Imam) replied, ‘I perform them in a sitting position only from the time I have gained this much weight and reached this age.’”
